9	\paragraph{Accuracy-range stability.} The \texttt{item\_id} variance share remains stable across subsets with mean accuracy from 0.62 to 0.72 ($r = -0.048$). This rules out distortion from binary floor or ceiling effects at observed accuracy levels.

11	\paragraph{Estimator robustness.} We compare Henderson Method~I with restricted maximum likelihood (REML-EM, 500 iterations, practical convergence $\Delta < 0.003$ percentage points). All budgets are conditioned on binary scoring; partial-credit analysis confirms that finer-grained rubrics require independent calibration (\S\ref{sec:binary}). We observe suggestive but underpowered format-associated differences warranting larger benchmark samples. Future work should extend to larger models, API-based systems, and continuous scoring metrics. Code, data, and a D-study calculator will be released upon publication.
